title: Graphite: the deposit rule as a kernel, pencil grades, pressure
description: Step 2 of docs/design.md. Tests for grain, saturation and conservation, with measured tone against pressure and against number of passes. Contact needs a random part per pass: the prototype's layers did not build tone. Sub-pixel coverage belongs here.
close_reason: Graphite grades, Sheet.stroke and the deposit kernel are in, with tests for grain, saturation and conservation

title: Paper and sheet: the state and the rendering of blank paper
description: Paper (texture, tooth size, depth, bite, colour) with presets; Sheet holding tooth, press, held and loose pigment; rendering by Kubelka-Munk over the paper, flat or raking light. Build order step 1 of docs/design.md.
close_reason: Paper, papers, Sheet and rendering are in, with tests

title: Design the core model: paper tooth, pigment deposit, media
description: Decide how paper (tooth height field, fibres), dry media (graphite, coloured pencil, charcoal, pastel, crayon, wax/oil-based) and their deposit, smudging, burnishing and erasing are represented, and how the result is lit. Reuse what fits from oilpaint (spectral Kubelka-Munk mixing, noise, PNG output). Add numba when the first kernel lands.
notes: Proposal in docs/design.md (branch core-model-design), with a prototype image. Waiting on four decisions: sharing code with oilpaint, units, names, where to start.
close_reason: Accepted: docs/design.md. Pixels, Sheet and Paper, graphite first; shared code in murex.

title: A shading helper: fill an area with strokes as a hand does
description: Shading only looks like pencil when the strokes do what a hand does: side by side at an angle, none quite straight or alike, lighter where the pencil lands and lifts. examples/pencils.py has such a function (shade); make it part of the library, with cross-hatching by shading again at another angle.
close_reason: Sheet.shade, with tests; examples/pencils.py uses it

title: Colour: coloured pencil and pastel, layering, wax, burnishing
notes: Revisit sanded card's tooth when pastel comes: with a pencil it covers only 57% of the sheet after many firm layers, because its tooth is mostly low with pointed peaks. Real sanded card takes pigment evenly.

title: Tips: wear, tilt, the side of a stick, crayon; graphite shine
notes: Tilt is built for round points (Sheet.stroke and Sheet.shade take tilt; the kernel's tip is an ellipse). Left for this step: wear, and the side of a charcoal or pastel stick, which is longer than a pencil's lead (SIDE is one constant, 5, for now: make it the medium's).

title: Dust: loose and held pigment, stump, erasers, charcoal
description: Step 3 of docs/design.md. The stump should leave streaks along its direction, not a clean blur.
close_reason: Charcoal, Sheet.smudge and Sheet.erase with stump, finger, chamois and erasers; press-in; tests for behaviour 3

title: Set up the project
description: Packaging (hatch, hatch-vcs, PyPI-ready metadata), uv, black, ruff, pyright, pytest, coverage with Codecov, cspell, tox, Makefile, CI, PyPI publish workflow, Dependabot, Beads, minimal AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md. Mirrors oilpaint.

title: Calibrate graphite tones against scans of real pencil
description: The constants of fusain/_engine.py were set so that tones land near figures estimated from experience (docs/design.md, One step of a stroke), not measured. Scan swatches of real 4H, HB, 2B and 6B on cartridge paper at a few pressures and numbers of layers, and fit the constants to them.

title: Extras: fixative, hatching helpers, ballpoint pen
description: Step 6 of docs/design.md. Ballpoint needs its own deposit rule: a paste laid at a steady rate.

title: Connect Codecov and PyPI trusted publishing
description: Human steps outside the repo: enable joce/fusain on Codecov (CI uploads with OIDC, no token), add a pending PyPI trusted publisher (project fusain, owner joce, repo fusain, workflow publish.yml, environment pypi) and create the pypi environment on GitHub with a required reviewer. See RELEASING.md.
close_reason: Codecov enabled (OIDC uploads), PyPI pending trusted publisher added, pypi environment has a required reviewer
